policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וַיֹּרוּ and ketiv ויראו are orthographic variants of the same verb (ירה, 'shoot'; the ketiv adds an aleph). ASV 'the shooters shot' renders that sense identically under either spelling and carries no italic supply or textual note on the unit; nothing in the English distinguishes the readings, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

Qere הַמּוֹרִים and ketiv המוראים are orthographic variants of the same participle (ירה, 'the shooters'; the ketiv adds an aleph). ASV 'the shooters' renders that sense identically under either spelling, with no italic supply or mapped textual note; the English does not distinguish the readings, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
